cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: A caching strategy defines who fills the cache and how writes keep it in sync. The default is cache-aside: read the cache; on a miss read the DB and store with a TTL; on write update the DB then delete the key.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Read-through lets the cache library load misses. Write-through writes cache and DB together: always current, slower writes. Write-behind writes the cache and flushes asynchronously: fast but can lose data. Write-around skips the cache for rarely read data. CDC fixes the dual-write problem.

questions.q: Why update the DB first, then delete the cache?
questions.a: Deleting first lets a concurrent reader reload and cache the old row before the DB write lands.
High write rates where a small loss window is fine, like counters, or with a durable log behind the cache.

questions.q: Why is cache-aside resilient to a cache outage?
questions.a: Reads fall back to the database; the cache is optional on the read path.
